meta.title: Learn SQL by Doing
meta.eyebrow: Study path, from the basics to performance
meta.subtitle: Queries, modeling and indexes using PostgreSQL
meta.description: A study roadmap for SQL with PostgreSQL, in eight weeks.
meta.tagline:
Learn by actually querying.
A local database and sample data.
meta.sidebarNote:
Write the query before looking at the answer.
A short daily session beats a long weekly one.

phases.title: Query data
phases.summary: Read data from one table and from several tables at once.

phases.title: Model and write
phases.summary: Create tables, relate them and change data safely.

phases.title: Performance
phases.summary: Understand why a query is slow and how to speed it up.

nodes.title: Local database and sample data
nodes.summary: Start a local PostgreSQL and load a data set to practice with.
nodes.challenge: Have a database running with at least three tables that contain data.
nodes.success: You can connect, list the tables and count the rows in each one.

tasks.title: Install PostgreSQL or start a container
Connect with psql or a GUI client
Count the rows in each table

nodes.title: SELECT, filters and sorting
nodes.summary: The basis of everything: choose columns, filter rows and sort the result.
nodes.challenge: Answer ten questions about the data using a single table.
nodes.success: You write the queries without copying examples.

nodes.title: Aggregates and grouping
nodes.summary: Summarize data: counts, sums, averages and groups.
nodes.challenge: Build a sales report by month and by category.
nodes.success: You explain the difference between WHERE and HAVING with an example.

nodes.title: JOINs
nodes.summary: Combine related tables without duplicating or losing rows.
nodes.challenge: List customers with no orders using a LEFT JOIN.
nodes.success: You predict how many rows a JOIN will return before running it.

tasks.title: Predict the row count before running
tasks.note: Write the prediction down and compare it with the result.

nodes.title: Subqueries and CTEs
nodes.summary: Break big queries into named, readable parts.

nodes.title: Create tables and types
nodes.summary: Define the structure of the data by choosing types and constraints.
nodes.challenge: Create the schema for a library with books, authors and loans.
nodes.success: The database rejects invalid data without help from the application.

nodes.title: Relationships and normalization
nodes.summary: Avoid repeated data and decide when to split it into another table.
nodes.challenge: Normalize a spreadsheet with repeated data into related tables.
nodes.success: You can justify every table and every key in your model.

nodes.title: INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE and transactions
nodes.summary: Change data safely and undo it when something goes wrong.
nodes.challenge: Implement a transfer between accounts that never leaves the balance inconsistent.
nodes.success: A failure in the middle of the operation does not leave half done data.

nodes.title: Views and functions
nodes.summary: Reuse queries and logic inside the database itself.

nodes.title: Indexes
nodes.summary: How the database finds rows, and when an index helps or hurts.
nodes.challenge: Create an index that brings a slow query from seconds down to milliseconds.
nodes.success: You explain why a specific index was chosen.

nodes.title: Execution plans
nodes.summary: Read the EXPLAIN output to find the bottleneck of a query.
nodes.challenge: Take three slow queries, find the cause of each one and fix it.
nodes.success: You point to the step in the plan that costs the most.

nodes.title: Window functions
nodes.summary: Rankings, running totals and comparisons between rows without losing detail.
nodes.challenge: Compute the monthly product ranking and the change from the previous month.
nodes.success: You solve it without nested subqueries.

nodes.title: Partitioning
nodes.summary: Split very large tables to keep queries fast.
